newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - BZW Metals sees firm copper price.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BZW Metals sees firm copper price.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices should remain firm for the rest of this year and look set to gain further ground over the five years, the chairman of BZW Metals and Energy Group said on Monday.

"If China emerges as a large buyer at some stage in the second half of this year and if in fact real consumption carries on, I see no reason why prices should not be firm in the months to come," chairman Christopher Green told Reuters at a meeting in Singapore partly organised by the Copper Development Centre.
"It very much depends on how China behaves in the second half of this year," Green said.
Reports have been swirling in the market that China has been selling copper to take advantage of prices on the LME, where the red metal recently hit a 13-month high above US$2,600 a tonne.

Green told delegates at the conference the "dramatic expansion in infrastructure demand" and a whole new generation of products containing copper in electronics and computers will underpin copper prices for up to the next five years.
"The so-called 'Tiger economies' of Southeast Asia were in the forefront of this expansion," he added.
The BZW Metals and Energy Group is part of BZW, the investment banking arm of Britain's Barclays Plc.

"I think we can safely reckon that world copper demand is now rising at a rate in excess of four percent per annum as opposed to the historical two or 2.5 percent," he said. "I see no reason to suppose that these rates of annual consumption will lessen over the coming years. Indeed, they may well accelerate."
"The producers are going to enjoy prices that will be substantially over US$1 a pound," Green said.

Much of the growth will also be fuelled by the expanding economy of China and to a lesser extent, India. There are also signs that countries in the former Soviet Union are beginning to recover from their previous economic slumps.
